sources.entry: HideNotch - Paints the menu bar black on MacBooks with a notch, so the notch blends in, and can round the screen corners.

summary.one_liner: HideNotch is a macOS menu bar app that paints the menu bar black on MacBooks with a notch so the notch blends in, and can round the screen corners.
summary.what_it_does: HideNotch paints the menu bar black on MacBooks with a notch so the notch visually blends into the bar. It can also add black rounded corners to the screen. A menu bar panel provides an on/off switch, a rounded corners toggle, and an option to paint the bar on external displays without a notch. When active, it also paints the bar (and corners) into a copy of the wallpaper so the bar stays black when macOS would otherwise show the wallpaper behind it once 10 or more windows reach the top of the screen. Turning it off or quitting restores the original wallpaper. The "..." menu offers launch at login, update checks, a website link, and hiding the menu bar icon. The README says it updates itself in the background.
use_cases: hide the notch on a MacBook
make the menu bar black on a notched MacBook
round the corners of the screen
keep the menu bar dark when many windows are open
paint the menu bar on an external monitor
install a menu bar utility via Homebrew
how_to_run: Or download HideNotch.dmg from the latest release
Open the dmg and drag HideNotch into Applications
Open HideNotch; it runs in the menu bar with no Dock icon
Click the menu bar icon and turn on the switch
notable: Paints the menu bar and wallpaper copy to keep the bar black even when macOS would show the wallpaper behind it (10+ windows at top of screen)
Can also paint the menu bar on displays without a notch
Automatically restores the original wallpaper when turned off or quit
Runs from the menu bar with no Dock icon
caveats: Notch remains visible on the lock screen and login window
Animated wallpapers such as Aerials cannot be painted, so the black bar fades out when 10 or more windows reach the top of the screen
Screen Time Downtime can hide the overlay; the README suggests adding HideNotch to Always Allowed, and restarting the Mac if it is not listed
